name: Bimetric Kinetic-Isolated Screened Aether (BIKISA)
claimed_mechanism: We exit the single-metric class via a Hassan-Rosen bimetric theory where the massive graviton breaks the diff-invariance slip-lock (DC-013). A standard-kinetic timelike vector u_mu supplies the required preferred-frame lensing slip, but its coupling to the metric is strictly screened by e^-y. The vector's longitudinal mode inherits a finite, independent kinetic normalization from a bare Maxwell-type stiffness, entirely decoupled from the screened e^-y coupling. This architecturally satisfies the A3 principle by preventing the screened PPN response from driving the propagating mode's kinetic normalization to zero (evading the P7 strong coupling wall that killed the khronometric and stiff-vector architectures).
predicted_weak_field: In the Solar System (y>>1), e^-y ~ 0, so the preferred-frame vector's coupling to the metric vanishes. PPN parameters revert to standard bimetric GR values (gamma=1, alpha_i=0), passing Cassini constraints. In the galactic halo (y<<1), the e^-y screen lifts, allowing the vector to mediate the off-ray lensing correction. Because the vector has a standard, independent kinetic term, it propagates as a healthy massive/massless spin-1 mode without strong coupling, yielding a clean, MOND-enhanced lensing ratio (Phi=Psi) and exact Newtonian MOND dynamics from the auxiliary chi field.
inequivalence_argument: This is structurally distinct from DC-001 (bimetric introduces a second metric, breaking the single-metric pincer), DC-010 (no khronon field; uses a standard kinetic vector), and DC-014 (the vector has standard, independent kinetic normalization, not a stiff/background field or a Proca mass normalized by e^-y). It avoids the P7 strong coupling by design, as the e^-y screening factor only multiplies the interaction term, leaving the canonical kinetic term of u_mu finite and independent.
